newsitem.title: USA: USAir settles three more Flight 1016 cases.
newsitem.headline: USAir settles three more Flight 1016 cases.

text.p: USAir on Thursday reached settlements in the cases of three more passengers who died in the 1994 crash of USAir Flight 1016, including one that was to have been presented to a federal jury Monday as an example case used as a guideline to help others settle.
All three plaintiffs were represented by Los Angeles lawyer Michael Baum. Neither he nor USAirways Group Inc would disclose the settlement amounts.
"These families feel that USAir has recognized their responsibility for this thunderstorm accident," Baum said.

The example suit was filed by the father of Ann Sharkey, a graduate student at the College of Social Work at the University of South Carolina, who was killed in the 1994 crash near Charlotte/Douglas International Airport in North Carolina.
The other two suits were filed by relatives of Paul Perez and Rita Gray, also killed in the crash.
No other cases filed in the U.S. District Court in Colombia were scheduled to go to court until May.
Last Friday, a federal jury found US Airways at fault in the crash, although it did not award punitive damages. US Airways settled five crash suits on Wednesday.
